newsitem.title: USA: Judge sets Hilton, ITT hearing date.
newsitem.headline: Judge sets Hilton, ITT hearing date.

text.p: A U.S. district judge has set a hearing date of April 17 for Hilton Hotels Corp's motion to require ITT Corp to hold its annual meeting in mid-May, a Hilton spokesman said on Wednesday.
The hearing will be held in Judge Philip Pro's courtroom in U.S. District Court in Las Vegas, Nevada, and it is scheduled to begin at 2:30 p.m. PST/5:30 p.m. EST.
Hilton launched a $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid for ITT in late January. ITT has rejected the bid and called it inadequate.

Hilton has asked the court to require the annual meeting so shareholders can vote on whether to re-elect ITT's current board or a Hilton nominated slate of directors. The Hilton-backed directors would then approve the Hilton acquisition offer.
In court papers, Hilton has argued ITT's bylaws and Nevada law require ITT to hold its annual shareholders meeting within one year of its previous meeting, which was in mid-May, 1996.

ITT has countered that its bylaws and Nevada state law do not require a mid-May meeting. Indeed, ITT claims it has 18 months from the previous date to hold its next meeting, which means it could have the meeting as late as November.
